title: Al-'Alaq: the first words
hookLine: read, in the name of your Lord who created you from a clinging clot, who taught by the pen (96:1–5)

lines: SOMEONE ELSE IS IN THE CAVE.
cards: A cave, high on a mountain outside Mecca, just big enough for one person to sit. A man of about forty climbs up there often, to be alone, to think, to turn toward God, with food his wife Khadijah has packed.
One night, according to Muslim tradition in the month of Ramadan, someone else is in the cave. What's spoken there becomes the first words of the Qur'an to be revealed.

teach.b: The story is told by Aisha in the opening pages of Sahih al-Bukhari. The angel Jibril came to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira and said one word: iqra'. Read, or recite.
The Prophet answered: I am not a reader. The angel pressed him tight, until he could bear no more, and said again: read. Three times.
Then came these words, in Pickthall's translation: Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth, Createth man from a clot.
Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous, Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not. 'Alaq, the word the surah is named for, means something that clings.
Pickthall says clot; many translators today prefer a clinging thing, and scholars discuss the range.

teach.h: A CLINGING THING, TAUGHT WHAT IT KNEW NOT.
teach.b: The point is the contrast: a human begins as something tiny and clinging, and is taught what he did not know. And notice the pen. The first revelation, to a man who said I am not a reader, is about reading and writing.
In the Qur'an's very first lines, knowledge is a gift from Allah.
The Prophet came down the mountain shaking, went home to Khadijah and said: cover me, cover me.
She wrapped him up, listened, and told him: Allah would never disgrace you. You keep ties with family, you help the weak, you honor guests, you stand by people in hardship.
The first person to believe him was the person who knew him best.

how: Muslims learn the story of the first revelation in the cave of Hira as part of the Prophet's life; the opening verses of Surah al-'Alaq are recited in the prayers and often quoted to honor learning.

o: the cave where the Prophet went to think
a clinging thing, what a human begins as
a quill used to write on parchment

games.q: who said what — tap the pairs.

s: the first revealed words were the opening of al-Fatiha
most scholars say the first were 96:1–5: read, in the name of thy Lord.
the first revelation mentions the pen
who teacheth by the pen, teacheth man that which he knew not.
Khadijah was frightened and sent him away
she wrapped him up, listened, and reassured him.

games.q: your husband comes down the mountain shaking, saying something happened in the cave. you're Khadijah. what do you do?
o: tell him to stop climbing up there
cover him, listen, and remind him of the good he does
games.why: she covered him and said Allah would never disgrace him: he kept family ties, helped the weak, honored guests (Bukhari).

practice: Find a pen and any paper, a receipt, the back of an envelope, or if you can't right now, trace the letters with a finger on your palm. Slowly write one thing you learned this week that you didn't know before.
Then sit with it: somebody taught you that, or something did.

wordCard.voice: Al-'Alaq. The clinging thing, the name of Surah ninety-six, whose first five verses were the first of the Qur'an revealed. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: read, or recite; the first word revealed, the same root as Qur'an.

carryVoice: Your line: taught by the pen. Everything you know, someone or something taught you. That's day one hundred eighty-one.

sources.q: Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous, Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.
